newsitem.title: UK: Oftel publishes BT interconnection proposals.
newsitem.headline: Oftel publishes BT interconnection proposals.

text.p: Britain's telecoms regulator said on Monday it had published proposals that would let British Telecommunications Plc set its own interconnection charges, subject to certain rules.

The Office of Telecommunications (Oftel), which currently sets BT's interconnection charges, said the proposals would replace the existing system of regulation with new arrangements that would give BT more pricing freedom.
Interconnection fees are the wholesale charges other operators must pay BT for the use of its network.
If agreed, the new arrangements would run from August 1997.
"The new framework will, in my view, meet the needs of the UK telecoms market in the future while retaining appropriate safeguards," director general Don Cruickshank said in a statement.
The proposals would allow BT to price competitive interconnection charges and would include pricing caps on some other services, Oftel said.
BT plans to merge with U.S. telecom MCI Communications Corp to create a global giant called Concert.
